title: Penguin Body Mass Across Groups
text:
Data: Palmer Penguins
In this post, I will look at how body mass varies across penguin species and sex, using the ‘palmerpenguins’ daatset.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins

penguins = load_penguins()

title: Penguin Body Mass Across Groups
text:
Visualising body mass by species

fig, ax = plt.subplots()

species_colors = {
    "Adelie": "tab:blue",
    "Chinstrap": "tab:orange",
    "Gentoo": "tab:green",
}

for species, group in penguins.groupby("species"):
    ax.scatter(
        group["flipper_length_mm"],
        group["body_mass_g"],
        label=species,
        alpha=0.7,
        color=species_colors[species],
    )

ax.set_xlabel("Flipper length (mm)")
ax.set_ylabel("Body mass (g)")
ax.legend(title="Species")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Body mass of penguins by species

title: Penguin Body Mass Across Groups
text:
Findings
Adelie and Chinstrap have similar findings, where they have both smaller body mass and smaller flipper length. Gentoo, however, has both a large body mass and large flipper length.

title: Penguin Bill Anatomy
text:
Data: Palmer Penguins, In this post, I will look at bill length and bill depth, and how they differ between the 3 species. I will also examine if you can determine a species from its bill shape alone.

library(palmerpenguins)
library(tidyverse)

title: Penguin Bill Anatomy
text:
Examining the data

penguins |>
    drop_na() |>
    glimpse()

Rows: 333
Columns: 8
$ species           <fct> Adelie, Adelie, Adelie, Adelie, Adelie, Adelie, Adel…
$ island            <fct> Torgersen, Torgersen, Torgersen, Torgersen, Torgerse…
$ bill_length_mm    <dbl> 39.1, 39.5, 40.3, 36.7, 39.3, 38.9, 39.2, 41.1, 38.6…
$ bill_depth_mm     <dbl> 18.7, 17.4, 18.0, 19.3, 20.6, 17.8, 19.6, 17.6, 21.2…
$ flipper_length_mm <int> 181, 186, 195, 193, 190, 181, 195, 182, 191, 198, 18…
$ body_mass_g       <int> 3750, 3800, 3250, 3450, 3650, 3625, 4675, 3200, 3800…
$ sex               <fct> male, female, female, female, male, female, male, fe…
$ year              <int> 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007…

title: Penguin Bill Anatomy
Penguin Bill Anatomy
text:
Visualising bill shape by species

penguins |>
    drop_na() |>
    ggplot(aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm, colour = species)) + 
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7) + 
    labs(x = "Bill length(mm)", y = "Bill depth (mm)") + 
    theme_minimal()







Figure 1: Bill length vs bill depth, coloured by species

title: Penguin Bill Anatomy
text:
Findings
Adelie has shorter bill lengths but larger bill depths, whilst Gentoo has larger bill lengths and shorter bill depths. However, Chinstrap has relatively large bill depth and bill length.

title: About
text:
Why Data Science?
My previous undergraduate research heavily involved Machine Learning, building a bridge between Chemistry and Data Science. However, majority of my previous experience was self taught. I struggled quite a bit during my research due to no actual machine learning guidance (no classes or anyone to teach me). Because of this, I decided a Masters in Data Science would significantly improve my skills and open up numerous opportunities in the future.
